originality.rationale: The Kabluchko–Thäle full primary paper addresses the identical 3-site spherical tessellation within its general f-vector program but supplies no cell-area distribution; the present theorem provides the full metric CDF, density and variance. Cho–Saul already establishes the angular Gaussian kernel lemma, which is not asserted to be new. Li et al. treat random query-to-fixed-site distance, not random cell area. Real external and available-ledger comparisons found no equivalent/stronger coverage, with priority risks stated.
residual_risks: The first-order angular Gaussian kernel used in the proof is known (Cho–Saul 2009).
An unlocated older treatment of spherical random lune opening angles might already imply the exact area law.
Historical search breadth and database indexing are not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The complete labelled-cell metric area CDF for the naturally minimal nontrivial three-site spherical random Voronoi tessellation is mathematically motivated, not a numerical curiosity. It exhibits genuinely varying area despite deterministic perimeter, exact variance, area covariance and sharp one-sixth sub-hemisphere probability. Previously published complete f-vector results do not determine this metric law.
